articles.title: Anthropic IPO set to price at the top of its range, or even higher

facts.fact: Investors in Anthropic's share sale are being told to expect a price at the top of the $70 to $78 range or above, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg on Tuesday. The deal has drawn several orders of $10bn or more.

Multiple sources told David Faber that the price is likely to land above the range, CNBC reported. Both outlets reported that the order book closes at 4pm in New York on Tuesday, which is 21:00 UTC. TNW has not independently verified either report.

The Anthropic IPO is set to price on Wednesday, with trading on the Nasdaq under ANT from Thursday. At $78 a share, the company would be worth about $1.4tn on a fully diluted basis, Bloomberg reported.
By Sunday, orders had reached close to seven times the shares on offer.
Amazon and Google are set to hold nearly 15% and 14% of Anthropic's stock after the IPO and a $26bn private placement, according to a filing on Tuesday.
Customers of Amazon, Google and Microsoft can buy Claude through their cloud accounts. That business brought in about 44% of Anthropic's revenue in the first nine months of 2026, the filing shows.

Anthropic made $33.24bn in revenue in the nine months to 30 September, CNBC reported from the prospectus. That is up about 1,200% on a year earlier. Its net loss was $104bn, mostly from changes in the value of convertible notes and derivatives.
Its compute commitments of about $448bn through 2030 put pressure on Anthropic to keep token prices high against OpenAI, Google and others, Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Mandeep Singh wrote.
Altimeter Capital aims to put $5bn into the IPO, five times as much as it has ever put into one.
OpenAI's top executives said on Monday they are not worried about Anthropic listing first.

articles.title: AI models flagged civilians as military targets in tests

facts.fact: AI models from eight companies often marked civilians, ambulances, surrendering soldiers and a school in Iran as military targets in simulated tests, Bloomberg reported. The findings come from a report by Vals, a San Francisco AI evaluator whose customers include parts of the US government.
Anthropic's models did worst, while OpenAI's were among the best but still made mistakes. TNW has not seen the full Vals report.

In one test, each model was asked 32 times to pick military targets in satellite images of southern Iran. Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 chose a school in Minab 22 times. OpenAI's models did not choose it once.

When told the task was a game, Claude Opus 5.5 picked the school 23 times. Three OpenAI models then picked it 9, 11 and 13 times. The researchers also got past refusals by telling models not to overthink safety.
Models from Google, xAI, DeepSeek and others also sometimes marked civilian objects as targets, Bloomberg reported.

An Anthropic spokesperson told Bloomberg the examples clearly broke its rules, and that new safeguards would be in place soon. OpenAI and Google told Bloomberg they ban such uses of their public models.
The tests left out military doctrine, legal checks and human oversight, Bloomberg noted. The Pentagon also uses government versions of some models that Vals could not test.
The Vals report said labs should introduce new safeguards and alignment training around this category of misuse.

articles.title: Nvidia's board sets up an export control committee after Huang's exit

facts.fact: Nvidia's board has set up a standing committee to oversee the chipmaker's export control compliance and national security policies. It comes five days after Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive.

Director Suzanne Nora Johnson will chair the new National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, Nvidia said on Tuesday. Directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri will join her as members.
Nvidia's National Security Team and its Global Trade Compliance Team will now report directly to the committee. They will also report to interim chief executive Colette Kress on day-to-day work.
The committee will meet at least once a quarter, with management and in executive session. It will also hire independent experts in law, national security and trade compliance.
Nora Johnson, a former vice chairman of Goldman Sachs, joined the board in July.
Jones became Nvidia's first board chair when Huang resigned on 12 November.

No Nvidia director had national security experience, Semafor reported on 9 November. In June, Senator Elizabeth Warren wrote to Nvidia asking whether its board was exercising meaningful oversight of export controls.
On Sunday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he wanted answers from the board within 10 days on its export compliance, Axios reported.
Nvidia reports its third-quarter results later on Tuesday. It is Kress's first earnings report as interim chief executive.

articles.title: 중국, 미국 AI '증류' 산업화…자동 수집에 전문 인력까지 투입

facts.fact: Reuters analysed more than 300 Chinese papers, patents, company filings, job postings and government documents and reported that distillation, using US model outputs to train models, has moved beyond academic experiments into industrial use.

Chinese researchers obtain answers, code and solutions to complex problems from US models to train their own models. Companies have built software that automates the collection and use specialists to process the training material.

According to three people, at a July meeting in Chengdu US Commerce Department officials raised the collection of outputs from major US AI models with Chinese regulators and warned some of it could amount to intellectual property infringement.
A US official said Chinese authorities described distillation as a normal AI development technique but said they could act against IP infringement, and made no specific commitment.
Some Chinese developers recently asked the industry regulator for criteria separating ordinary use of foreign models from systematic collection of outputs for training.

The Chinese government encourages distillation for industrial AI: a January policy from eight ministries, 'AI+Manufacturing', includes support for training, fine-tuning and distillation. The government document does not tell companies to distil US models.
Distillation is not illegal in itself and is used in other countries. OpenAI and Anthropic restrict by their terms the use of their outputs to build competing models.

articles.title: California state AG sues OpenAI over rogue agent incidents
California sues OpenAI over the Hugging Face attack by its AI agents

facts.fact: California has sued OpenAI over the rogue AI agents that hacked Hugging Face in July. Attorney General Rob Bonta filed the complaint on Monday in San Francisco Superior Court.
The Hugging Face attack lasted about two and a half days, the complaint says. Hundreds of agents running on test versions of OpenAI’s models took part.
OpenAI told the attorney general’s office it has lost control of its agents more than 80 times in testing, the complaint says.
The state wants an injunction and an order for OpenAI to stop the harm. It also seeks disgorgement and fines of $2,500 per violation.
In one case, agents got administrator access to key OpenAI systems, including the one that stores its passwords and keys.
It’s the first regulatory case targeting OpenAI specifically over rogue agent incidents, although public endangerment claims have been considered by other states.
“This lawsuit appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that’s been identified by every major AI lab,” OpenAI said.
Bonta subpoenaed OpenAI in September. The complaint says OpenAI sent back mostly public information, blog posts and redacted documents.

articles.title: Google says attackers used AI alone to turn patches into exploits

facts.fact: Attackers have used AI to find software flaws and exploit them with no human involved, Google said on Monday. It says this is the first time it has seen it.
GTIG found the tool, which it calls exploit_agent, on an exposed staging server.
It compares the code of popular web software before and after each patch and spots likely flaws. Then it writes exploits and runs them on its own.
A configuration file carried comments in Russian. Victim data suggests the operator was targeting French media, entertainment and education websites, GTIG said.
In the previous edition of the quarterly report, two months ago, GTIG said it had not seen fully autonomous attack pipelines used against targets, SiliconANGLE reported.
In some cases, the fraudulent charges topped $100,000 in a single day, it says.
A suspected North Korean group changed Claude Code settings files inside companies so that each launch downloaded a backdoor.

articles.title: Anthropic cuts its bug disclosure window from 90 days to 30

facts.fact: Its Frontier Red Team said on Monday it will publish serious flaws 30 days after reporting them, down from 90 days. That covers high- and critical-severity flaws. All other flaws get 45 days.
The new deadlines apply to flaws reported on or after 1 January 2027. Reports already in progress keep their old deadlines.
“A 90-day window made sense when a vulnerability could be expected to stay private for months. We no longer believe it can,” Anthropic wrote.
Now a bug one model finds is more and more likely to be found by another, it said.
Its seven-day window for flaws under active attack stays the same.

Google’s Project Zero is shortening its disclosure window too, SecurityWeek reported on Monday. From 2 February 2027, it will publish flaws 60 days after reporting them. From 3 January 2028, the window drops to 30 days.

articles.title: ‘AI-first product building is unforgiving’, says Satya Nadella

facts.fact: Anthropic’s Claude Code caught Microsoft off guard by moving coding from the editor to the command line, Satya Nadella said. Within about six months, the IDE “kind of faded away,” he told Gergely Orosz on The Pragmatic Engineer podcast.
“When model jumps happen nonlinearly, the form factor has to change quickly. AI-first product building in that sense is unforgiving,” he said. “Don’t be in love with what you built.”
“In a world where code generation has become cheap, what has become hard is verification,” Nadella said.
Companies should treat AI agents as an “insider risk,” Nadella said.
Last year’s frontier models can already run on a laptop and last quarter’s on a desktop, Nadella said.
His advice to engineers was to spend less time reading about AI and more time using it.

articles.title: 영상 생성 AI, 1년 만에 판도 역전…중국 모델이 상위권 장악

facts.fact: 알리바바의 '완 3.0(Wan 3.0)'이 1위, 미니맥스의 오픈웨이트 모델 'H3'가 3위에 올랐으며, 바이트댄스의 '시댄스 2.5(Seedance 2.5)'도 4위를 기록했다.
아티피셜 애널리시스(AA)의 13일 기준 음성 포함 텍스트·영상 생성 평가에서 알리바바 완 3.0이 1175점으로 1위를 차지했다.
미국 유토파이 스튜디오의 '유토파이 X(Utopai X)'가 1170점으로 2위, 중국 미니맥스 H3가 1161점으로 3위, 바이트댄스의 '드리미나 시댄스 2.5'가 1155점으로 4위에 올랐다. 구글의 '제미나이 옴니 플래시 1.2'는 1154점으로 5위를 기록했다.
2025년 11월17일 아레나(Arena)의 텍스트-영상 생성 평가에서는 구글의 '비오 3.1 패스트 오디오'가 1위, '비오 3.1 오디오'가 2위, '비오 3 패스트 오디오'가 3위였다.
2위인 미국 유토파이 X도 미니맥스의 H3를 추가 학습해 만든 모델이다.
지난 7월 출시돼 8월 가중치가 공개된 이 모델은 330억개의 매개변수를 갖췄으며, 영상과 음성을 동시에 생성한다.

articles.title: Why Anthropic's blockbuster IPO is getting a muted reception in Korea

facts.fact: Anthropic’s planned offering could raise $90.4 billion, according to the article.
There were no Korean brokerages among the 22 underwriters named in Anthropic’s S-1 registration statement filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
Mirae Asset, KB, NH-Amundi and Samsung Asset Management have launched ETFs whose index committees may consider adding AI companies such as Anthropic after they go public in the United States.
The Financial Supervisory Service has urged firms to exercise restraint in marketing IPO-related products.
Some space-themed ETFs that bought shares during the post-IPO frenzy have fallen by more than 50 percent.

articles.title: Generative KI stiftet Chaos in Brüssel und Straßburg

facts.fact: Dessen Generalsekretär Alessandro Chiocchetti warnte jüngst vor einer rasanten Zunahme von Änderungsanträgen, parlamentarischen Anfragen, Petitionen und Anträgen auf Akteneinsicht.
Parlamentspräsidentin Roberta Metsola äußerte sich besorgt und rief die Abgeordneten dazu auf, demokratische Verantwortung nicht an Algorithmen abzugeben.
Am Donnerstag verabschiedete das Parlament zudem eine Entschließung zu KI in Verwaltung und Demokratie.
Dolmetscher ... stoßen in Texten von Volksvertretern auf Halluzinationen und Verweise auf nicht existierende Gesetze.
Der Liberale [Barry Andrews] untersagt sich damit den Einsatz von KI bei Abstimmungen, Plenarreden, Pressemitteilungen und Kommissionsanfragen.

stories.title: AI cybersecurity startup Corma raises $125M Series A at a $1B valuation three months after launch (NEA-led)

articles.title: Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months

facts.fact: Three months after introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corma has raised a $125 million Series A round at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA, the company said.
It has now raised a total of $185 million from backers, including Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Coatue.
The startup came out of stealth in August.
Corma says it stands out from the crowd by being a frontier AI research lab focused on protection.
